135 relief camps ready as Sabari rises in Polavaram district

In Polavaram district, authorities have prepared 135 relief camps in anticipation of potential flooding as the Sabari river continues to rise. The preparedness measures come amidst concerns over increasing water inflows into both the Sabari and Godavari rivers, which could impact a significant number of communities.

A total of 161 villages situated along the riverbanks are identified as likely to be affected should water levels continue their upward trend. District administration and emergency services are closely monitoring the situation, ready to respond to any escalation. The primary focus remains on ensuring the safety and well-being of residents in vulnerable areas.

As part of the precautionary actions, 101 pregnant women residing in the potentially affected regions have been specifically advised to make preparations for shifting to hospitals. This measure aims to ensure they receive timely medical attention and care, mitigating risks associated with potential displacement or difficult access during a flood event.

Authorities are maintaining constant vigilance over water levels and weather forecasts to guide further actions. The establishment of relief infrastructure highlights a proactive approach to disaster management in the face of rising river flows. Community leaders are also engaging with residents to disseminate information and ensure compliance with safety advisories.

What to watch: Authorities will continue to monitor river levels and potential for further inflows.

Bangladesh launches measles vaccination drive amid deadly outbreak

Bangladesh has launched a comprehensive month-long measles vaccination drive, implemented amid an ongoing and deadly outbreak of the disease. The initiative represents a critical public health response to safeguard vulnerable populations across the nation.

The campaign specifically targets children aged from 6 months to 59 months. This group includes young individuals who may have previously missed their scheduled immunisation efforts. A significant change in policy for this drive is the lowering of the minimum vaccination age. Authorities have reduced it from the usual 9 months to 6 months, a direct consequence of the severity of the current measles outbreak. This adjustment aims to provide protection to younger infants earlier than typically prescribed.

The primary objective of this intensive immunization program is to curb the spread of measles and reduce the morbidity and mortality associated with the deadly outbreak. Health authorities are urging parents and guardians to ensure their eligible children receive the vaccine during this crucial period. The concentrated effort over a month signifies the urgency with which the government is approaching the public health crisis.

This nationwide campaign underscores Bangladesh's commitment to protecting its youngest citizens from preventable diseases, especially in the face of a heightened health threat. Its success will be vital in bringing the current measles situation under control and preventing future outbreaks.

FINANCE · Livemint Money · editor 10/10 · 1 min read fact-checked

Understanding Passive Investing: A Guide for Savers

For ordinary savers and taxpayers, understanding investment strategies is key. Passive investing offers a distinct approach compared to more active methods. With passive investing, funds are designed to track market indices. This means that instead of relying on individual stock selection by a fund manager, your money follows the performance of a broad market benchmark, such as a stock market index. This method significantly reduces the need for constant individual stock picking and analysis. For an ordinary saver, this approach can mean a simpler way to participate in the market. It removes the burden of researching and selecting individual companies, as the investment aims to mirror the market's overall movement. This can be appealing for those who prefer a less hands-on approach to their investments, focusing on capturing market returns rather than attempting to outperform the market through specific stock selections. It provides a way to gain broad market exposure without the intensive management associated with active investment strategies.

What to watch: Consider how different investment strategies align with your financial goals.

SCIENCE · Phys.org · editor 10/10 · 1 min read fact-checked

Molecular 'self-destruct' switch discovered: How stressed cells decide between survival and death

Researchers at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev (BGU) have identified a crucial molecular switch within human cells, shedding new light on how stressed cells determine their fate. This discovery reveals the mechanism by which cells either activate a survival pathway or initiate programmed cell death, known as apoptosis.

The findings, recently published in the scientific journal Redox Biology, describe a precise molecular control point. This switch dictates whether a cell, when under stress, will attempt to repair itself and survive, or if it will trigger its own demise. Understanding this intricate cellular decision-making process is a significant step forward in cell biology.

The implications of this research extend beyond fundamental science. The BGU team suggests that these insights could be instrumental in addressing a major challenge in cancer treatment: chemotherapy resistance. Aggressive tumors often develop mechanisms to evade the cell-killing effects of chemotherapy, making treatment less effective.

By understanding how this molecular switch operates, scientists may be able to manipulate it to force cancer cells into apoptosis, even when they are resistant to current therapies. This potential to overcome resistance could pave the way for more effective treatments for various forms of aggressive cancer, offering new hope for patients.

What to watch: Further research into manipulating this switch for targeted cancer therapies.

Source: Phys.org · permalink · more science

SCIENCE · Phys.org · editor 10/10 · 1 min read fact-checked

Digital textbooks significantly boost students' intrinsic learning motivation

A collaborative research effort by teams from The Education University of Hong Kong (EdUHK) and East China Normal University (ECNU) has delivered compelling evidence on the benefits of digital textbooks (DTs). Their comprehensive meta-analysis concludes that digital textbooks significantly enhance students' intrinsic learning motivation when compared to traditional paper textbooks.

The study, which synthesized data from a substantial body of prior research, offers a robust statistical confirmation of DTs' positive impact. The meta-analysis encompassed 27 experimental and quasi-experimental studies conducted over a 24-year period, from 2000 to 2024. This extensive review involved a total of 3,590 participants, lending considerable weight to its conclusions.

The findings suggest that the interactive and dynamic nature often associated with digital learning materials plays a crucial role in engaging students more deeply. Intrinsic motivation, which stems from internal satisfaction and interest in learning, is a key factor in academic success and lifelong learning. The significant boost observed indicates a powerful pedagogical advantage for digital formats.

This research provides valuable insights for educators, curriculum developers, and policymakers considering the integration of technology into learning environments. As educational institutions continue to evolve, the demonstrated ability of digital textbooks to foster greater student engagement and motivation presents a strong case for their widespread adoption and further development.

What to watch: How these findings influence educational policy and digital textbook design.

POSITIVE · The Better India · editor 10/10 · 1 min read fact-checked

Goa’s Blueprint for Ending Rabies: A Replicable Model

While rabies remains a persistent threat across India, the state of Goa has successfully eliminated human rabies, offering a concrete blueprint for other regions. This achievement was not accidental but the result of a structured, three-module approach that addresses the disease at multiple points simultaneously. The first module focuses on immediate response. Since 2014, a 24/7 hotline has coordinated care for bite victims, ensuring standardized, free treatment including post-exposure prophylaxis at all government facilities, removing financial barriers to life-saving care. The second module targets the source of infection by systematically vaccinating free-roaming dogs. By tracking coverage with precision, Goa reached the critical threshold of 70% vaccination in specific areas, effectively breaking the chain of viral transmission. The final module focuses on prevention through education. Rabies awareness was integrated into the state science curriculum for grades 11 and 12, reaching over 150,000 community members annually. This long-term strategy ensures that future generations understand the critical first 15 minutes after a bite. The results are profound: human rabies deaths dropped from 17 in 2014 to zero by 2018, while canine cases fell by 92%. An independent analysis confirmed the program is highly cost-effective. This model requires no unique infrastructure, only disciplined implementation of existing protocols, making it a viable path for India’s broader national efforts to achieve rabies-free status.

Why it matters: Goa’s success proves that integrated, cost-effective public health strategies can eliminate deadly zoonotic diseases, providing a replicable template for the rest of India.

Source: The Better India · permalink · more positive

SCIENCE · Phys.org · editor 10/10 · 1 min read fact-checked

Harnessing Phages: A New Library for Combating Bacteria

An estimated 38 trillion bacteria reside within the human body. While the vast majority of these microorganisms are harmless or even beneficial, a small fraction can cause serious illness. The challenge intensifies when these harmful bacteria develop resistance to standard antibiotics, rendering conventional treatments ineffective and leaving patients vulnerable to severe infections.

In response to growing antibiotic resistance, scientists are turning to bacteriophages, often called phages, which are viruses that specifically infect and kill bacteria. These biological agents offer a targeted alternative to broad-spectrum antibiotics. By constructing a “library” of diverse phages, researchers aim to identify and deploy specific viral strains capable of neutralizing particular resistant bacterial strains.

This approach leverages the natural specificity of phages, which typically target only certain bacteria without harming the surrounding beneficial microbial community. Unlike antibiotics, which can disrupt the broader microbiome and promote further resistance, phage therapy offers a precise mechanism for eliminating pathogenic bacteria. As the global health community seeks sustainable solutions to the crisis of multi-drug resistant pathogens, the development of comprehensive phage libraries represents a significant step forward. These resources allow for the rapid matching of phages to specific bacterial threats, potentially restoring the efficacy of infection control measures in clinical settings. The focus is on creating a robust, accessible repository of these viral tools to address the escalating threat of untreatable bacterial infections.

What to watch: The expansion of phage libraries and the integration of phage therapy into clinical protocols for resistant infections.

Source: Phys.org · permalink · more science
